mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings and increasing the present value of equities, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months, or the average return in such periods is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% over a 3-month window signals weakening labor market conditions, which increases the likelihood of central bank rate cuts to stimulate growth, thereby boosting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX fails to generate positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential investment (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in private demand, which increases the probability of fiscal or monetary stimulus, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of interaction-triggered instances, or the joint signal has a Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in real output, which increases the likelihood of central bank intervention to prevent recession, thereby lifting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in fewer than 50% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the year-over-year growth of GDP (GDPC1) above 3.0% signals strong economic momentum, which increases corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX fails to generate positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the CPIAUCSL above 237.5 with a 12-month growth rate exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflationary pressure, which increases the probability of aggressive monetary tightening, leading to higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in fewer than 55% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 140,000 and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.7% signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and the likelihood of Fed rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX fails to produce negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of interaction-triggered instances, or the joint signal has a Rank IC < -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in residential construction (HOUST) below 1000 for two consecutive months, combined with a drop in consumer spending (RSAFS) below 445000, indicates a collapse in private demand, which increases the probability of fiscal stimulus and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 1000 and RSAFS < 445000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX fails to generate positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the interaction signal has a Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.
